behavioral_notes.observation: Overrides mrp's _cal_price: after super() values the consumed component moves, it sums work_order._cal_cost() across all workorder_ids (labour = duration x workcenter.costs_hour) plus extra_cost x qty, giving total_cost = sum(consumed move.value) + work_center_cost + extra_cost. It then splits total_cost onto byproducts by their cost_share % and sets price_unit on the finished move_finished_ids to (total_cost x (1 - byproduct_cost_share/100)) / quantity. Only applies for fifo/average cost_method (standard-cost products keep standard_price). This price_unit is what stock_account then writes into the finished-goods stock.valuation.layer.

After stock_account's _post_inventory creates the component-consumption and finished-goods stock.valuation.layers, _post_labour fires for MOs that reach state 'done' (real_time valuation + a production-location valuation_account_id required). It buckets each workorder's _cal_cost() by workcenter.expense_account_id (fallback product expense account), then creates and _post()s a single balanced account.move on the product's stock_journal: debit per expense account, credit the production location's valuation_account_id (workcenter_cost capitalised into the produced goods). Each resulting account.move.line is written back onto the workorder's mrp.workcenter.productivity.account_move_line_id (idempotency guard: skipped if time_ids already linked). This is the labour-cost GL posting metadata cannot show.

Override on production moves: returns value = quantity x price_unit (the price_unit set by _cal_price) with a production-scoped description ('<value> for <qty> <unit> from <MO>'). This is the hook stock_account calls to compute the finished/byproduct stock.valuation.layer amount for a manufacturing output, replacing the generic incoming-cost logic. _get_kit_price_unit / _get_all_related_sm additionally value phantom (kit) BoM outputs by exploding the kit and summing component price_units so kits are not double-counted.

On _compute_duration / _set_duration the workorder recomputes value = -(duration/60) x workcenter.costs_hour and, when the workcenter carries an analytic_distribution, creates/updates account.analytic.line rows via account.analytic.account._perform_analytic_distribution. Lines are tagged category='manufacturing_order', product_uom hours, ref=production.name, and stored on wc_analytic_account_line_ids; they are unlinked on workorder action_cancel/unlink. This posts shop-floor labour cost onto the analytic (cost-centre) ledger independently of the financial GL postings.

The WIP wizard (account.group_account_manager) collects in-progress MOs (state progress/to_close/confirmed) and posts a Work-In-Progress journal entry: credit stock valuation account for picked component value (lot/standard_price x qty), credit the overhead account for workorder _cal_cost, and debit the company account_production_wip_account_id for the total. It immediately books a reversing entry on reversal_date (default next day) so the WIP sits on the balance sheet only at the cut-off date. Both moves carry wip_production_ids back to the MOs and surface on mrp.production.wip_move_ids.

Recomputes a manufactured product's standard_price from its BoM: sums operation costs (opt.cost) + each bom_line component standard_price x qty, recursing into child BoMs, then nets byproduct cost_share and divides by bom.product_qty. Exposed via the product/template 'Compute Price from BoM' button (button_bom_cost) and list action. product.category gains property_stock_account_production_cost_id (the production valuation counterpart account used for both components and finished goods); res.company excludes kits from valuation and product._compute_value zeroes kit valuation to avoid double counting.

MO Overview shows the real done-move unit cost (move._get_price_unit) instead of the planned cost. The stock valuation report is patched to add a 'Cost of Production' section aggregating the valuation of production-usage stock locations (the WIP/labour capitalised value) when any production location has a valuation account.

2 JS files, 1 XML template, 0 OWL components, 0 registry adds; patches StockValuationReport.prototype + StockValuationReportController.prototype to render the added 'Cost of Production' block; bundle ['web.assets_backend'].

side-effect: mrp.production._post_inventory/_post_labour -> posts labour account.move (DR expense, CR production valuation account) + links mrp.workcenter.productivity.account_move_line_id

side-effect: mrp.account.wip.accounting.confirm -> posts + reverses a WIP account.move (component + overhead vs production_wip account)
side-effect: product.product._set_price_from_bom -> rolls BoM component + operation cost into product standard_price

classification.rationale: mrp_account is a cost-accounting bridge, not a primary transform: it does not move material or convert inputs (that is mrp + stock), it records the financial consequences of manufacturing into the ledger and the cost (analytic) accounting layer. It is the support glue between the 'make' value chain (mrp) and the financial system of record (account / stock_account): _cal_price values the finished-goods stock.valuation.layer, _post_labour capitalises workcenter cost into the GL, work-order analytic lines feed the cost-centre ledger, and the WIP wizard books work-in-progress at period cut-off. Under Stabell & Fjeldstad / Porter this is firm-infrastructure support (auto_install=true onto mrp+stock_account). It maps to APQC 9.0 Manage Financial Resources — specifically 9.3 Perform cost / management accounting (analytic manufacturing cost) and 9.x inventory/product costing & valuation — feeding, not performing, the 4.3 Produce/Manufacture primary activity its parent mrp owns.

capturing direct labour / workcenter overhead into product cost

Whether/when the WIP wizard is run in practice vs left to manual period close, and how its reversal interacts with the real labour move posted at MO done.
Interplay with stock_account anglo-saxon vs continental valuation configs for the production valuation counterpart account.
